name: English Language & Comprehension
overview: English is the fastest and most predictable section of SSC CGL: 25 questions for 50 marks in Tier 1 (2 marks each, negative 0.5) and 45 questions for 135 marks in Tier 2 (3 marks each, negative 1). The syllabus splits into three families. **Vocabulary** — synonyms-antonyms, one-word substitution, idioms and spelling — is a pure memory bank of roughly 400 high-frequency items that recycles year after year; a prepared candidate answers 7-9 questions in under 4 minutes. **Grammar application** — error spotting, sentence improvement, fill-in-the-blanks, active-passive and direct-indirect — runs on a fixed set of rules (subject-verb agreement, tense sequence, articles and prepositions, the voice and narration tables) that never surprise. **Comprehension** — reading comprehension, cloze test and sentence rearrangement — rewards a daily reading habit more than any technique. Unlike Quant or Reasoning, almost nothing here is ambiguous: every question has one defensible answer under standard grammar, which is why toppers treat English as the section to finish first and score 45+ out of 50 in Tier 1.
strategy:
## The one-line plan

**Bank the vocabulary, memorise the tables, read daily** — vocabulary is a memory problem, grammar is a table problem, and comprehension is a habit problem; none of the three rewards last-minute problem-solving.

## Priority order for preparation (max ROI first)

1. **Grammar backbone (grammar-essentials)** — subject-verb agreement, tenses, articles, prepositions, pronouns, conditionals. Every error-spotting, improvement and cloze question secretly tests one of these rules; one week here pays rent for the whole section.
2. **Active-passive and direct-indirect** — two pure-formula topics worth 2-5 questions a shift. The eight-row voice table and the four-check narration protocol are one evening's memorisation each, and the marks are permanent.
3. **Vocabulary bank (synonyms-antonyms + one-word substitution)** — ~250 words + 120 one-word items with a daily quota (see plan below). This alone secures 3-5 questions per shift.
4. **Idioms and spelling** — 130+ idioms in family clusters and 90+ trap words; 15 minutes a day for a month covers both, and Tier 1 almost always pays 2-3 questions for it.
5. **Error spotting + sentence improvement** — apply the grammar backbone with a fixed checking order; 4-6 questions between them every shift.
6. **Cloze test** — passage-level grammar and collocation; the strategy (read the whole passage, fit grammar before vocabulary, use connector logic) converts it into easy marks.
7. **Reading comprehension** — 2-3 questions per passage restated from the text (detail, vocabulary-in-context) and 2-3 that need the author's stance (main idea, inference, tone). Practice matters more than theory.
8. **Sentence rearrangement** — one PQRS jumble in Tier 1, several paragraph jumbles in Tier 2; the pair-linking method makes it a 40-second item.
9. **Fill in the blanks** — collocations and phrasal verbs; revise alongside the vocabulary bank.

## The vocab daily plan (non-negotiable 20 minutes)

- **10 new synonyms + 10 antonyms** from the topic banks, each used in one spoken sentence of your own. Recognition fades; production sticks.
- **10 new idioms** in family clusters (animals, colours, food, situations, people) — one sentence each.
- **5 one-word substitutions**, learned with their suffix logic (phobia-, -cide, -phile, -logy, -archy).
- **Anything missed twice goes to a bleeder list** — a 15-20 item sheet revised every Sunday. Most permanent marks come from this list, not from new words.
- Every 7th day: no new words; revise all 7 days + the bleeder list.

## The reading habit plan (non-negotiable 20 minutes)

- **Daily:** read one newspaper editorial (The Hindu / Indian Express or any serious English daily) in 15 minutes. After reading, write — do not think, *write* — three lines: the author's main claim, the author's tone, and one sentence summarising the argument. This trains the exact muscles RC questions test: main idea, inference and tone.
- **While reading:** mark 5 unfamiliar words; add them to the vocabulary quota above. Editorial vocabulary overlaps the SSC word bank heavily.
- **Weekly:** one full RC set untimed (analyse every wrong answer against the passage), then one set timed at 45-50 seconds per question. Analysis, not attempting, is where the marks come from.

## Time budget

- **Tier 1:** 25 questions in 18-20 minutes. Budget: vocabulary sweep 4-5 min, voice + narration 2 min, error/improvement/fill 6 min, cloze 3 min, rearrangement 1.5 min, RC 4-5 min. English underwrites the other sections — never let it eat Quant's time.
- **Tier 2:** 45 questions in ~35-40 minutes as part of the combined module; RC sets arrive as two 5-question blocks, so read each passage once and answer all five from it.

## Attempt order inside the section

1. **Vocabulary sweep** — synonyms, antonyms, idioms, one-word substitution, spelling: instant-recognition items, 25-35 seconds each. Bank 7-9 questions before the clock is felt.
2. **Voice + narration** — pure formula; the tables settle them in 30 seconds each.
3. **Error spotting + improvement + fill in the blanks** — grammar application; run the fixed rule-sweep on each.
4. **Cloze test** — read the full passage once, then answer blank by blank.
5. **Sentence rearrangement** — pair-linking elimination.
6. **Reading comprehension last** — the only items that can eat variable time; attempt them with whatever remains, detail questions before inference questions.

## Accuracy targets

- Tier 1: attempt all 25 with **90%+ accuracy** — English expects full attempt; 45+ out of 50 is the standard topper line and 40+ is comfortably achievable with the banks in this course.
- Tier 2: attempt 42-45 of 45; the 3-mark question size makes every skip expensive, but the negative marking makes blind guessing on inference items wasteful — eliminate two options first.
- In vocabulary items there is no excuse for a wrong answer after the banks are done; in RC items, never pick an option because it sounds wise — pick it because the passage supports it.

## Practice protocol

Daily: 20 questions from the current topic + 10 mixed questions from topics finished more than a week ago (spaced repetition beats cramming). Weekly: one full Tier 1 English section in 20 minutes and one Tier 2 set, reviewed question-by-question — keep an error log with one line per mistake: *bank gap* (word not known), *table slip* (rule misapplied) or *reading miss* (answer contradicted the passage). Bank gaps go into the bleeder list; table slips go into a 10-minute rule drill; reading misses mean slow down on RC inference questions. After each mock, recompute your section time split — most candidates need two cycles to move RC to the end without rushing it.
